description: Compare two as-designed records — the design-vs-design sibling of the reconcile family, which only ever compares design against reality. Findings are directional relative to the named base: `added` / `removed` / `changed` (property-level), banded into design content vs the supporting layer (change events, questions, provenance). Pass base_path alone to compare the live graph against a committed export ('has this session diverged from the record?'); pass other_path too to compare two export files (branches, machines, alternatives). Reports divergence, never judges which side is right. On a server that holds many designs (a registry behind a trusted host) pass other_graph_id instead of a path: the live graph is the base and the other design is read by graph_id from the one the server holds, inside the set of designs the host says you may read; a path is not served there.

base_path.description:
Path to the base export document — what every finding is relative to
(`added` = in the other side, not here). Typically the committed
export, or the main branch's copy of it. Required unless
`other_graph_id` is passed, which makes the live graph the base.

budget_chars.description:
How many characters of JSON this reply may spend before prose is
withheld to make it fit (default 30,000). See `reply_budget`: counts and
ids are never budgeted away, so a shorter answer is never a quieter one.

other_graph_id.description:
The other design BY GRAPH_ID, on a server that holds many designs (a
registry behind a trusted host): the live graph is the base, labelled
by this design's graph_id, and the other design is read from the one
the server already holds, inside the set of designs the host says you
may read. Not combined with a path; refused on a single-design server,
and for a design outside that set.

other_path.description:
Path to the other export document. Omit to compare the live graph as
the other side — "has this session diverged from the record?".

name: compare_designs
title: Compare Two Designs
